entry.title: Cheetah family
entry.summary: A cheetah and her cubs on a kill in the long grass, watching the sky between bites.

entry.title: Elephant and guineafowl
entry.summary: An elephant under a lone tree and a guineafowl up in the branches, Serengeti.

entry.title: Lions in the tree
entry.summary: Two lions resting up in the branches of a tree, the Serengeti's tree-climbers.

entry.title: Odd corners
entry.summary: A fire extinguisher on the plain, a bare acacia, and a serval: the Serengeti's odd corners.

entry.title: Giraffe and hippos
entry.summary: A giraffe among the acacias and hippos packed into a shrinking waterhole, Serengeti.

entry.title: Zebra, morning
entry.summary: Zebra in early Serengeti light, kept in colour and black and white.

entry.title: On the plains
entry.summary: Zebra in the open and a lone antelope on the rocks, between the bigger Serengeti sightings.

entry.title: Lions, mid-afternoon
entry.summary: A pride in the afternoon heat, one male asleep and a lioness on the move.

entry.title: First drive, Serengeti
entry.summary: The first hours in the Serengeti: wildebeest on the track, a leopard in the grass, gazelles at a distance.

entry.title: At the pumps
entry.summary: A rider at a roadside fuel stop leaving Lake Natron, kept in colour and black and white.

entry.title: Escarpment light
entry.summary: The last of the dawn near Lake Natron, from the camp to the light on the escarpment.

entry.title: Dawn, Lake Natron
entry.summary: Sunrise over the plain near Lake Natron, the volcano and the sky and a figure by the truck.

entry.title: The volcano and the stream
entry.summary: Ol Doinyo Lengai across the plain with a green stream leading in, and the banded rock of a nearby gorge.

entry.title: The ground at Lake Natron
entry.summary: Mineral crusts, a footprint in the mud, and the salt flats running out to the shore at Lake Natron.

entry.title: Flamingos, Lake Natron
entry.summary: Flamingos in the shallows and a figure crossing the flats at Lake Natron, mid-morning glare.

entry.title: Under the mountain
entry.summary: Morning on the plain near Lake Natron: a giraffe, the volcano, and a gathering of Maasai.

entry.title: Acacia under Lengai
entry.summary: A flat-topped acacia stacked against the volcano with the long lens, colour and black and white.

entry.title: Beadwork and blue
entry.summary: More Maasai portraits from the morning near Lake Natron, colour and black and white.

entry.title: Maasai, morning light
entry.summary: Morning portraits in Maasai country near Lake Natron, each kept in colour and black and white.

entry.title: Shuka at dusk, Lake Natron
entry.summary: A figure wrapped against the evening chill near Lake Natron, in black and white and colour.

entry.title: Acacia and the volcano
entry.summary: A lone acacia on the plain and Ol Doinyo Lengai beyond, late on the road to Lake Natron.

entry.title: Toward Lake Natron
entry.summary: Late light on the drive north: a giraffe, gold hills, and long-horned cattle in the grass.

entry.title: Village crafts, Lake Natron
entry.summary: A banana flower, a basket weaver, a palm mat: a village stop on the road to Lake Natron.

entry.title: Maasai portrait, near Lake Natron
entry.summary: The first Maasai portrait of the trip, on the road toward Lake Natron, kept in colour and black and white.

entry.title: By the window, Arusha
entry.summary: A woman resting a moment by a market window in Arusha, in black and white and colour.

entry.title: At the stall, Arusha
entry.summary: A young man reaching up to the grille of a market stall in Arusha, kept in both black and white and colour.

entry.title: Arusha market
entry.summary: Faces and colours from the market at Arusha, mid-afternoon before leaving town.

entry.title: Glass mosaics, Arusha
entry.summary: Leaf and vine mosaics in cut glass, set into a wall at a craft gallery near Arusha.

entry.title: Carved masks, Arusha
entry.summary: A wall of carved and painted masks at a craft gallery near Arusha.

entry.title: Vervet monkeys, Arusha
entry.summary: A pair of vervet monkeys moving through the branches above the lodge, first day in Tanzania.

entry.title: Lodge garden, Arusha
entry.summary: The first morning in Tanzania, spent in a garden near Arusha before the drive north.

entry.title: The Loire, low water
entry.summary: The Loire at Chaumont in August, sandbars exposed and a single flat-bottomed boat in the channel.

entry.title: The chateau
entry.summary: Chateau de Chaumont-sur-Loire at the end of the day, its turrets above deep flower borders.

entry.title: Alstroemeria, twice
entry.summary: Two stands of alstroemeria from the domaine's borders, one orange, one pink, both streaked and freckled.

entry.title: Leaves, up close
entry.summary: Foliage at the domaine: monkey puzzle, a backlit canna leaf, a rubber plant's red new growth, and scarred bamboo.

entry.title: Water gardens
entry.summary: Ponds at the festival: yellow and pink water lilies, horsetail reeds, and glass dragonflies set among the rushes.

entry.title: Larger gestures
entry.summary: Sculptural plots at the festival: a carved mask on a post, a blue water wall, and a shingle-scaled form winding to a pool.

entry.title: Woven and wrapped
entry.summary: Material studies from the show gardens: bound bamboo, a hanging screen of woven cones, and a canopy of paper squares.

entry.title: Small worlds
entry.summary: Three storybook plots at the garden festival: a fairy house in the reeds, floating painted tiles, and a hollow tree laid for tea.

entry.title: Boats and a watcher
entry.summary: Show gardens at Chaumont-sur-Loire: blue boats stranded on gravel, and a hooded figure standing in the planting.

entry.title: Carved wood, low light
entry.summary: Contemporary wood sculpture in a vaulted room at the Domaine de Chaumont-sur-Loire, lit so the shadows carve too.

entry.title: Vendome, early evening
entry.summary: Coneflowers, a half-timbered house over the Loir, and firecracker vine in the last of the sun.

entry.title: Four windows
entry.summary: Light through the glass at the Abbaye de la Trinite, Vendome, from medieval saints in the apse to a mid-century abstract.

entry.title: The tower and the cloister
entry.summary: The Abbaye de la Trinite in Vendome: a freestanding Romanesque bell tower above a cloister of willow beds and worn stone.

entry.title: Céret, the modern note
entry.summary: A last stop in Céret, the little Cubist town: bolts of Catalan striped cloth, and a contemporary gallery of felt cylinders and glass block.

entry.title: Collioure
entry.summary: The town that pulled in Matisse and Derain: its waterside bell tower, the fort on the hill, and the old stone streets running down to the sea.

entry.title: Garden greens
entry.summary: The leaves rather than the flowers: a jade plant against a warm wall and the fresh growth on a young araucaria.

entry.title: Banyuls, boats and cellars
entry.summary: A morning in Banyuls-sur-Mer: painted Catalan fishing boats hauled up ashore, an old winery chimney, and a quiet cove at the end of the coast.

entry.title: Garden, in flower
entry.summary: After a week of fortresses and facades, a morning among the flowers: bird of paradise, powderpuff, and alstroemeria in the southern warmth.

entry.title: The JOB building, outside in
entry.summary: More of the JOB building in Perpignan: a bronze against gold mosaic, the ochre facade, and a loggia opening onto its planted courtyard.

entry.title: The JOB building
entry.summary: Inside the JOB building in Perpignan, the Art Nouveau headquarters of the cigarette-paper firm: an ironwork staircase, painted murals, and gilded panels.

entry.title: Cathédrale Saint-Jean
entry.summary: Inside Perpignan's cathedral: a tall stained-glass window over a gilded altar, and a rose window set high in the shadow of the vault.

entry.title: Le Canigou
entry.summary: The snow still on Canigou in May, rising over the greenhouses and market gardens of the Roussillon plain.

entry.title: The coast, last light
entry.summary: A working harbour on the Côte Vermeille, and the one proper sunset of the week over a rocky cove.

entry.title: Vineyards to the sea
entry.summary: Late light on the Côte Vermeille, where the vineyards are terraced right down to the cliffs and a hill town catches the last of the day.

entry.title: Perpignan facades
entry.summary: The city's early-twentieth-century architecture: a bold orange villa, a blue-and-yellow house, and the Art Nouveau ironwork of the old Caisse d'Epargne.

entry.title: Perpignan, three ways
entry.summary: An afternoon across Perpignan: a street-art Dali, the vast marble cloister of the Campo Santo, and a Maillol bronze in the town-hall courtyard.

entry.title: The palace chapel
entry.summary: The royal chapel of the Palais des Rois de Majorque: a star-painted vault, worn frescoes, and stained glass holding the last of the light.

entry.title: The palace, inside
entry.summary: The great hall of the Palais des Rois de Majorque, a deep window onto the Canigou, and the small details underfoot.

entry.title: Palais des Rois de Majorque
entry.summary: The fortified hilltop palace of the medieval kings of Majorca, in Perpignan: a brick ramp, a galleried courtyard, and a chapel framed in a Gothic arch.

entry.title: Leucate, before the rain
entry.summary: The lagoon and marina at Leucate as a storm built over the coast, and a modern church holding its own against the sky.

entry.title: Inside Salses: the dark rooms
entry.summary: Deeper into the fortress, where the light runs out: a brick tunnel, an arcaded passage, and a vaulted chamber lit by one small window.

entry.title: Inside Salses: the courtyard
entry.summary: Within the walls of the fortress: an oven cut into the stone, a courtyard with its own well, and brick arcades running off into shadow.

entry.title: Forteresse de Salses
entry.summary: A late-medieval Spanish fortress in pink brick, built low and squat to survive the artillery age. Still standing guard over the Roussillon plain.

entry.title: Côte Vermeille, grey morning
entry.summary: The rocky coast near Banyuls under low cloud: coves, umbrella pines, and a single yacht far out on a flat sea.

entry.title: Arrival, Roussillon
entry.summary: First evening in French Catalonia. A dog with a lake to himself and a cat with the best seat in the village.

entry.title: The Haverthwaite line
entry.summary: A maroon steam tank engine easing under an iron footbridge, the driver leaning out. Last morning on the Lakeside and Haverthwaite Railway.

entry.title: The house on the point
entry.summary: A house set on its own wooded promontory at the southern, quieter end of Windermere, still water in front.

entry.title: Slate and blue
entry.summary: Evening light on a slate-built church and its old headstones, the window frames picked out in blue.

entry.title: Windermere from the water
entry.summary: A big house on the far shore, the wooden launches at their jetties, and the lake wide and quiet. Windermere from its edges.

entry.title: Bowness Bay, morning sun
entry.summary: The same bay a few days on, this time in morning sun: rowing boats bright on the shingle, swans working the shallows.

entry.title: Rydal Water, clear hour
entry.summary: Rydal Water under the one blue sky of the trip: reed-fringed, low islands, the fells out at last.

entry.title: Grasmere's fleet
entry.summary: Painted hire boats moored along the shore at Grasmere, a swan working the waterline. Waiting for the season to start.

entry.title: Stone, two ways
entry.summary: Stepping stones set across a beck and a drystone wall along a field edge. Two old uses of Lakeland stone.

entry.title: In the woods above the lake
entry.summary: A great mossy beech and an old ice house cut into the bank, found on a path above the water.

entry.title: Lambs, late April
entry.summary: Ewes and this year's lambs in a green valley field, cherry blossom just opening. Spring comes late to the fells.

entry.title: Grasmere, first morning
entry.summary: A yacht on flat grey water and a pointed fell rising over the cottages. The first morning in Grasmere, under cloud.

entry.title: Garden to dusk
entry.summary: Pale tulips in the afternoon, the same tulips at dusk, and the sun finally dropping under the cloud over the fells.

entry.title: Swaledale
entry.summary: A horned Swaledale ewe on cropped green grass, deciding whether I was worth moving for.

entry.title: Windermere, four moods
entry.summary: One grey afternoon on the shore of Windermere: a stony foreshore, two jetties, and a bare lakeside tree holding its ground.

entry.title: The wishing log
entry.summary: A fallen trunk studded with coins hammered edge-on into the grain, turned copper and green with age. A Lakeland habit, one coin at a time.

entry.title: Rowing boats, Bowness Bay
entry.summary: Wooden hire boats pulled up on the shingle at Bowness in the rain, red keels showing, the launches waiting behind.

entry.title: Bowness, in red
entry.summary: A phone box above the rooftops and a Triumph Stag by the Belsfield hedge. Two reds, five minutes apart.

entry.title: Last frames, Japan
entry.summary: A wall of apartment balconies glowing on the last night, then people riding the escalators up behind a glass front the next afternoon. The last two frames of the trip.

entry.title: Tokyo from the top
entry.summary: Fuji cut out on the orange horizon, the Sumida threading the city in lit bridges, a single floodlit ball field burning in the dark. Tokyo from the top of the Skytree as the sun went.

entry.title: The Skytree, day to night
entry.summary: The tower from the street with a crane for company, straight up the lattice, the blue guts of it, then lit green and gold after dark. Back where the trip started, this time going up.

entry.title: The bridge at dusk
entry.summary: The old green truss lit amber against a deep blue sky, the lamps coming on, the river town behind. Kanazawa, and the trip, signing off.

entry.title: Omicho Market
entry.summary: A bed of local oysters on ice with the prices stuck in, baskets of seaweed down the side, the whole covered arcade humming under green and yellow awnings. Kanazawa's kitchen.

entry.title: Kenrokuen at dusk
entry.summary: A yukitsuri cone doubled in the still pond with the sunset behind it, a stone lantern lit in the trees. The last of the day at Kenrokuen, the garden at its quietest.

entry.title: Rigging for winter
entry.summary: Yukitsuri, the rope cones that hold Kenrokuen's pines up under heavy snow, going on tree by tree. A man up a ladder, and the finished cones against the dusk.

entry.title: Kenrokuen, up close
entry.summary: Wet red maple, a pine branch holding its drops, fallen leaves over the moss, one last branch glowing against the dark. Kenrokuen in pieces as the light went.

entry.title: Kenrokuen, late autumn
entry.summary: A rainbow over the castle hill with the trees gone gold, then the garden ponds holding the maples upside down. Kenrokuen in late autumn, the weather doing the work.

entry.title: After dark, Kanazawa
entry.summary: Glass towers, a hotel bar high over the lights, a negroni built slow, an empty escalator running gold. The contemporary side of Kanazawa, late at night.

entry.title: Warm windows, Kanazawa
entry.summary: The Tsuzumi-mon over the station's glass dome, a sake shop glowing with bottles, a restaurant front full of coloured glass. Kanazawa after dark.

entry.title: The ryokan room
entry.summary: A round window cut straight onto a single pine, the interior all warm lamp and the garden going blue behind the glass. First night in Kanazawa.

entry.title: Nightcap, Kyoto
entry.summary: A green one on a dark bar at the end of the day, beside a bottle of Japanese pearl liqueur with the blue settled at the bottom like sediment. A long way from the temples.

entry.title: Dusk over Kyoto
entry.summary: The sun catching the cloud above the Higashiyama hills, then full dusk from the slope with the city lights coming up and Kyoto Tower the one lit needle in the murk.

entry.title: Pagoda over the city
entry.summary: Up close the temple is all painted joinery in blue, green and gold; from across the valley, just a red tower above Kyoto. Kiyomizu's pagoda as the light turned.

entry.title: Up to Kiyomizu
entry.summary: A rainbow over the Higashiyama rooftops on the climb up, then the city framed through the vermilion pillars and the pagoda with half of Kyoto at its feet. Kiyomizu in the late sun.

entry.title: Kennin-ji, afternoon
entry.summary: A big Zen hall behind clipped pines, a thatched teahouse among turning maples, and a bronze pilgrim by the bell. A quiet afternoon at Kennin-ji, Kyoto's oldest Zen temple.

entry.title: Dressed for the shrine
entry.summary: A family in their best for shichi-go-san, the boy in blue holding still, and two women under the big stone torii with a parasol up against the sun. A Kyoto shrine on a November morning.

entry.title: Yasaka Shrine
entry.summary: The big cypress-bark hall, a couple in formal dress reading their fortune on a red bench, and a chozuya where the water runs straight onto the moss. A quiet morning at Yasaka.

entry.title: Kamo River, into Gion
entry.summary: Walking in along the Kamo River with the machiya backed up to the water, then into Gion as the light came through. First morning in Kyoto.

entry.title: Last light around the walls
entry.summary: The park gone red and gold along the moat, a tower catching the sunset across the water, then the keep over the ramparts with the crows coming in. The last of the light, and of the trip.

entry.title: From the top of the keep
entry.summary: The city going gold to the mountains, and one of the castle's golden shachihoko in the corner, the rooftop ornament you usually only see from below. The view from the top of Osaka Castle.

entry.title: Osaka Castle
entry.summary: The moat with the old stone wall on one side and the Business Park towers on the other, then the keep itself, gold in the low sun. An afternoon at Osaka Castle.

entry.title: The escalator tube
entry.summary: A glass escalator tube slung between the two towers, blue-lit ribs the whole way and the gold of the next floor at the end. The best bit of the climb up the Umeda Sky Building.

entry.title: Umeda Sky Building
entry.summary: The ring lit gold, the escalators crossing the gap, the sky bridge glowing blue, then the city it was built to look at, laid out in the dark. Up the Umeda Sky Building after sunset.

entry.title: Umeda after dark
entry.summary: The Christmas illuminations just up in front of Osaka Station: the street trees lit purple, then round the corner the crowd by the cinemas and a long rank of bicycles.

entry.title: Behind glass
entry.summary: A katana in a gold-lacquer scabbard, resting on cream silk and lit out of the dark. The last frame of the trip, and the quietest.

entry.title: Two ways of looking out
entry.summary: A tatami room framing a moss garden and a stone lantern, then Kengo Kuma's glass at the Nezu Museum. The same idea, centuries apart.

entry.title: A neighbourhood, early
entry.summary: A Don Quijote tower, a timber-clad Starbucks in a winter wreath, a green-tiled apartment block with a spiral stair. The ordinary texture of Tokyo, before the day got going.

entry.title: Out late
entry.summary: A yakiniku place lit up yellow and red with nobody on the street, then a bar alley two minutes away, warm and crowded with signs. Tokyo after ten.

entry.title: Dusk, and the way out
entry.summary: The thatched teahouse on the pond going quiet, then out past the hoardings where the towers caught the last of the sun. Closing time at Hamarikyu.

entry.title: Hamarikyu, the water
entry.summary: The tidal pond holding the city upside down, towers going gold as the sun dropped. The wooden bridge, the pines, the same skyline doubled in still water.

entry.title: Hamarikyu, golden hour
entry.summary: The garden's black pines kept low and broad over the grass, Shiodome's towers standing just past the treeline. Hamarikyu as the light went gold.

entry.title: The loose hour
entry.summary: Two kids parked on the grass with the towers behind them, then an empty side street with the sun coming in low. The unstructured part of an afternoon.

entry.title: Two in kimono
entry.summary: Two visitors in rented kimono near the palace, happy to stop for a frame. One small thing gives the century away.

entry.title: Around the Imperial Palace
entry.summary: The moat with the city stacked along one bank, the clipped black pines of the outer garden, then Nijubashi. A loop where the towers never quite leave the frame.

entry.title: From the KITTE roof
entry.summary: Tokyo Station's red brick seen from above, platforms fanning out behind it, glass towers all around. The Marunouchi rooftop everyone climbs up for, and the reason why.

entry.title: Tokyo International Forum
entry.summary: Up out of the underground passages and into Viñoly's glass hall, where the ceiling lifts away into a lattice of white ribs. The way in mattered as much as the room.

entry.title: Garden pond, morning
entry.summary: Clipped shrubs, a maple turning, the still water doing the rest. A small Tokyo garden first thing, with the city standing in close behind the hedge.

entry.title: At the counter
entry.summary: A single piece of silver-skinned nigiri on a bamboo leaf, ginger and scallion on top, gari beside it. The sign behind promises Ōma tuna; this came first.

entry.title: An atrium cat and a quiet staircase
entry.summary: A cat in a spacesuit piloting a rocket over a shopping atrium, then a travertine staircase quiet as a chapel. Two interiors a minute apart, opposite moods.

entry.title: Ginza to Marunouchi, Sunday afternoon
entry.summary: A man in a Louis Vuitton kimono owning a Ginza crossing, then a red postbox and a building wearing its garden, a few blocks over in Marunouchi. Three frames from one walk.

entry.title: Skytree from the bridge
entry.summary: The tower is nominally the subject, but the sky took up most of the frame, and most of the work.

entry.title: Chairs as portraits
entry.summary: Two chairs lit from behind in their cases at Designmuseum Danmark, photographed straight on like portraits: an Eames LCW in molded plywood, and Arne Jacobsen's blue Lily with its curling arms.

entry.title: Morning at the Glyptotek
entry.summary: Two from the Glyptotek on a quiet morning: Kai Nielsen's marble water mother in the planted Winter Garden, and a visitor who happened to match the rose walls of the painting rooms.

entry.title: Copenhagen, late evening
entry.summary: Two from the same golden hour: a window where the harbor and a wall of portraits overlap in reflection, and Nyhavn with the light running along the old fronts.

entry.title: Copenhagen harbor, evening
entry.summary: Three from the inner harbor on a late-June evening: new housing on the Christianshavn waterfront, the Opera House across the water, and the fountain in front of it where two children were deciding how close to get. The light this far north holds long past dinner.

entry.title: Copenhagen, behind the street
entry.summary: Three spaces a few minutes apart: a courtyard reached through a dark gateway, the spiral ramp of the Round Tower, the glass dome at the Glyptotek. The city does a lot with the light it lets in slowly.
